acceptance: The Presto-family 1_v7 rewrite uses one array of ROW values (alignment intrinsic) and, by the harness at a recorded clean commit, passes at SF1, SF2 and SF3 on Trino 476 under stock limits (1.80 GB per node on a 6 GiB heap) with results equal to canonical Q1 within 1e-8

Peak user memory per run is recorded for each scale and compared with the 0.75-0.93 GiB per SF baseline in _project/audits/tpchavoc-q1-array-scale-2026-10-22.md; the ORDER BY keep-or-drop decision is made from those harness numbers
tests/unit/tpchavoc/test_presto_compat.py structural assertions describe the new shape for presto, trino and athena dialects
The 1_v7 variant description or docs state that memory is linear in rows of the largest Q1 group, and the owner decision on a documented requirement versus a scale-gated skip is recorded
description: The 1_v7 rewrite for Presto and Trino (four ordered ARRAY_AGG columns unnested together) exceeds Trino's default per-node memory limit from SF2: it passes at SF1 at about 800 MiB but fails with EXCEEDED_LOCAL_MEMORY_LIMIT at SF2, SF3 and SF10, while canonical Q1 needs under 16 MiB. Memory is linear in rows, about 0.75-0.93 GiB per scale factor, dominated by HashAggregationOperator ARRAY_AGG state. See the remedy spec in the context of tpchavoc-q1-array-scale-check and _project/audits/tpchavoc-q1-array-scale-2026-10-22.md. Indicative probes showed one ARRAY_AGG of ROW values cut peak memory about 1.7-1.9x, whereas chunking by GROUP BY or UNION ALL slicing gave no reduction. This does not make memory bounded; it moves the stock-limit break from about SF2 to about SF4. Do not claim more.
